::Fraser welcomes you with a supercilious smile.:: Corporal, Corporal... how good of you to show up - and just at the right time. There is a package waiting for you. ::He produces a medium sized box with Protectorate markings and places it on the counter.:: It arrived from North Underrail a few hours ago.
Now, what could be inside, Corporal? Hmm?<end>

segment.source:
::As you open the package, you are surprised to discover that it contains a full Chemical Assault Unit armor set, complete with the instantly recognizable and equally petrifying mask the unit is known for. Beneath all of that, you find a small note that simply reads, "No rest for the wicked." Staff Sergeant Fraser curiously observes you unraveling your unexpected present and quirks an eyebrow upon seeing what it contains.::
Oh! I can see you have *really* earned the sympathies of Captain Mareth. Ah, Corporal, Corporal... I don't know how you do these things, but I salute you! That armor looks... mighty terrifying; I wish I had one in my possession, to be perfectly honest. ::He smirks.::<end>

segment.source: Anything else, Corporal?<end>
segment.target: Anything else, Corporal?<end>

segment.source: Do you work with SGS credits, by any chance?<end>
segment.target: Do you work with SGS credits, by any chance?<end>

segment.source: SGS credits? Oh, no, only charons and united stations dollars, I'm afraid.<end>
segment.target: SGS credits? Oh, no, only charons and united stations dollars, I'm afraid.<end>

segment.source: You know, perhaps I should have mentioned that earlier, but I had forgotten you were from SGS. Heh, that is one remote place; I couldn't imagine myself ever wanting to go that far south, unless it gets a bit more "northernized". No offense. ::He smirks.::<end>

segment.source: Colonel told me to see you about my pay.<end>
segment.target: Colonel told me to see you about my pay.<end>

segment.source: Here you go, Corporal, these blues are now yours. ::He gives you 250 United Stations dollars.::<end>
segment.target: Here you go, Corporal, these blues are now yours. ::He gives you 250 United Stations dollars.::<end>

segment.source: Heh, go get yourself something nice. You deserve it.<end>
segment.target: Heh, go get yourself something nice. You deserve it.<end>

segment.source: I'm here for my pay.<end>
segment.target: I'm here for my pay.<end>

segment.source: I came to collect my pay, Staff Sergeant.<end>
segment.target: I came to collect my pay, Staff Sergeant.<end>

segment.source: Heh... yes. I was informed of that. Let's see... two missions plus a bonus... That would be six hundred dollars, Corporal. That's a lot of blues... ::He smirks before continuing.:: What did you do, annihilate the Free Drones? Faceless? ::He laughs.::<end>
segment.target: Heh... yes. I was informed of that. Let's see... two missions plus a bonus... That would be six hundred dollars, Corporal. That's a lot of blues... ::He smirks before continuing.:: What did you do, annihilate the Free Drones? Faceless? ::He laughs.::<end>

segment.source: Actually, I decimated Free Drones' main base in South Underrail, sir. Or annihilated, if you really prefer that term.<end>
segment.target: Actually, I decimated Free Drones' main base in South Underrail, sir. Or annihilated, if you really prefer that term.<end>

segment.source: ::Fraser's smirk contracts into confusion and shuts him up for a brief moment. It doesn't last long, however.:: Well... I wasn't told anything about that yet. Strange. Truly.<end>
segment.target: ::Fraser's smirk contracts into confusion and shuts him up for a brief moment. It doesn't last long, however.:: Well... I wasn't told anything about that yet. Strange. Truly.<end>

segment.source: Um, here are your blues, Corporal. ::He hands you 600 United Stations dollars. His stare flees yours and hides in a chart he just picked up.::<end>
segment.target: Um, here are your blues, Corporal. ::He hands you 600 United Stations dollars. His stare flees yours and hides in a chart he just picked up.::<end>

segment.source: Consul Oliver told me to see you.<end>
segment.target: Consul Oliver told me to see you.<end>

segment.source: Corporal... Corporal... $(context.player.Name). Yes, I indeed have something for you here. Lots of blues, in fact.<end>
segment.target: Corporal... Corporal... $(context.player.Name). Yes, I indeed have something for you here. Lots of blues, in fact.<end>

segment.source: ::He counts and hands you 300 United Stations dollars.:: That's three hundred, Corporal. Heh, you must've done something to really please the good consul. Spend it well.<end>
segment.target: ::He counts and hands you 300 United Stations dollars.:: That's three hundred, Corporal. Heh, you must've done something to really please the good consul. Spend it well.<end>

segment.source: Why did you join the Protectorate?<end>
segment.target: Why did you join the Protectorate?<end>

segment.source: Corporal, Corporal... That is a good question. I joined the Underrail Protectorate to become a part of the mightiest military machinery this violent world of ours had ever seen. I was born in the North, the homeland, and felt a great... hmmm, the word eludes me... a great appeal to this idea of unifying the whole Underrail under a single, powerful rule.<end>
segment.target: Corporal, Corporal... That is a good question. I joined the Underrail Protectorate to become a part of the mightiest military machinery this violent world of ours had ever seen. I was born in the North, the homeland, and felt a great... hmmm, the word eludes me... a great appeal to this idea of unifying the whole Underrail under a single, powerful rule.<end>

segment.source: No offense, but the South is not really the most sophisticated region of Underrail, isn't it true? You ought to know it better than me. Bandits, murderers, Lunatics... Tchortists? What's up with that? As your kind would say it, South Underrail seems pretty derailed to me. It needs discipline, whether the simple folk want it or not.<end>
segment.target: No offense, but the South is not really the most sophisticated region of Underrail, isn't it true? You ought to know it better than me. Bandits, murderers, Lunatics... Tchortists? What's up with that? As your kind would say it, South Underrail seems pretty derailed to me. It needs discipline, whether the simple folk want it or not.<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about the Free Drones?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about the Free Drones?<end>

segment.source: I think you know enough about them, Corporal.<end>
segment.target: I think you know enough about them, Corporal.<end>

segment.source: ::He picks up another chart and begins inspecting it.::<end>
segment.target: ::He picks up another chart and begins inspecting it.::<end>

segment.source: Heh, Free Drones. I don't see what the big deal is about them; they are but a minor nuisance to us. Protectorate is strong enough to... wipe the ground with these anarchists.<end>
segment.target: Heh, Free Drones. I don't see what the big deal is about them; they are but a minor nuisance to us. Protectorate is strong enough to... wipe the ground with these anarchists.<end>

segment.source: Corporal, Corporal... I've already heard about the Rail Crossing situation, and I know what you did. If one - no offense - simple Southerner can stand in their way, then... Well, you understand, don't you?<end>
segment.target: Corporal, Corporal... I've already heard about the Rail Crossing situation, and I know what you did. If one - no offense - simple Southerner can stand in their way, then... Well, you understand, don't you?<end>

segment.source: Did you just call me simple?<end>
segment.target: Did you just call me simple?<end>

segment.source: No, Corporal, you must be hearing things. Besides, I don't like that tone of yours. That's not how you talk to a superior officer.<end>
segment.target: No, Corporal, you must be hearing things. Besides, I don't like that tone of yours. That's not how you talk to a superior officer.<end>

segment.source: I have other questions.<end>
segment.target: I have other questions.<end>

segment.source: I'm not going anywhere.<end>
segment.target: I'm not going anywhere.<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about Colonel Cathcart?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about Colonel Cathcart?<end>

segment.source: An outstanding man. A truly brilliant commander, and a friend of mine, if I may say so. You've met him yourself, Corporal, I think you should've realized that by now. How can one not?<end>
segment.target: An outstanding man. A truly brilliant commander, and a friend of mine, if I may say so. You've met him yourself, Corporal, I think you should've realized that by now. How can one not?<end>

segment.source:
I could go on and on about him, but I'll choose to be concise: Without him, Underrail Protectorate wouldn't have any presence in the South. I've been here during the crucial moments, where subtle moves meant you stay in the game or you get kicked out; he played the moves right.
That's all you need to hear from me.<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about Consul Oliver?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about Consul Oliver?<end>

segment.source: The consul is our compatriot, a true Northerner: Educated, intelligent, honest... a good-natured man. Perhaps even too good-natured sometimes. This is South Underrail after all, and here you have to have your claws sharpened, whether you come as a Protectorate soldier or a United Stations diplomat.<end>

segment.source: Most Southerners are so... unrefined and decadent, Corporal. Diplomacy gets incredibly difficult when you're dealing with people who aren't on the same level as you.<end>
segment.target: Most Southerners are so... unrefined and decadent, Corporal. Diplomacy gets incredibly difficult when you're dealing with people who aren't on the same level as you.<end>

segment.source: You have a problem with Southerners?<end>
segment.target: You have a problem with Southerners?<end>

segment.source:
Corporal... Corporal. Really now, I don't know where you got that idea. I was merely talking about *certain* Southerners, the ratters. Please...
You and your ideas. ::He laughs.::<end>
segment.target:

segment.source: What can you tell me about Luka?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about Luka?<end>

segment.source: Heh... Wait, who are you talking about? ::He pauses for a second.:: Luka... Luka... You mean that fat mechanic?<end>
segment.target: Heh... Wait, who are you talking about? ::He pauses for a second.:: Luka... Luka... You mean that fat mechanic?<end>

segment.source: ::He erupts into laughter.:: How funny of you to *actually* think I'd socialize with someone like him! Ah... Anyway, I can't tell you anything at all about the man, Corporal. He is... under the radar to me, so to say.<end>
segment.target: ::He erupts into laughter.:: How funny of you to *actually* think I'd socialize with someone like him! Ah... Anyway, I can't tell you anything at all about the man, Corporal. He is... under the radar to me, so to say.<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about Anastasia?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about Anastasia?<end>

segment.source: Corporal, that woman is a diamond. She is a far greater hero than any one of us here, no matter how surprising that might seem to you. Her train was assaulted by the Free Drones, those barbarians, and they hurt her. And she was traveling to Fort Apogee to help our soldiers. And her reward for such a big heart? She suffered chemical burns on her body as well as pernament voice damage from the toxic gas.<end>

Her train was assaulted by the Free Drones, those barbarians, and they hurt her. And she was traveling to Fort Apogee to help our soldiers. And her reward for such a big heart? She suffered chemical burns on her body as well as pernament voice damage from the toxic gas.<end>

segment.source: Heh, and do you know what she did after that, Corporal? Do you? She carried on. She knew brave Protectorate soldiers needed her help and she stayed here all these years, despite being offered to return to the homeland and retire. All on Protectorate expense.<end>

segment.source: It takes true bravery and commitment to do that, Corporal. She's a true Northerner and an inspiration to us all.<end>
segment.target: It takes true bravery and commitment to do that, Corporal. She's a true Northerner and an inspiration to us all.<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about Case?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about Case?<end>

segment.source: ::He sighs.:: Look, Corporal, if you feel the need to ask me about various people from Fort Apogee, ask about someone important... and someone who's not a ratter, preferably. Especially not someone who is named Justin. Case. ::He laughs.::<end>

segment.source: What a stupid name. Oh, well, what would you expect...<end>
segment.target: What a stupid name. Oh, well, what would you expect...<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about CAU?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about CAU?<end>

segment.source: You've met Captain Mareth, I see. I admire that man, greatly, as well as his whole unit. They are highly trained in small arms combat, hand-to-hand combat, demolitions, chemical weapon combat - obviously ... What more can I say?.<end>
segment.target: You've met Captain Mareth, I see. I admire that man, greatly, as well as his whole unit. They are highly trained in small arms combat, hand-to-hand combat, demolitions, chemical weapon combat - obviously ... What more can I say?.<end>

segment.source: Ah, Corporal... Corporal, I remember one time when they were dispatched from the homeland... When was it... Two, three years ago? I met him, he was a lieutenant back then, and a marvelous man he was. Highly intelligent and to-the-point kind of man. Highly disciplined. All their missions here, as I recall, were done with great precision and efficiency.<end>

segment.source: Heh, now that I think of it... they should come here more often. They are efficient.<end>
segment.target: Heh, now that I think of it... they should come here more often. They are efficient.<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about the Faceless?<end>
segment.target: What can you tell me about the Faceless?<end>

segment.source: They are not to be toyed with, Corporal, and we all understand it. They never made any hostile moves against us, at least not directly, but Port Zenith in Core City is under Protectorate control, and if the Faceless make the wrong move, they might just taste the bitter end of it. We are ready for everything, as always.<end>

We are ready for everything, as always.<end>

segment.source: The South is really a freak show, isn't it? But, you know this very well already, so that comment was redundant, I suppose.<end>
segment.target: The South is really a freak show, isn't it? But, you know this very well already, so that comment was redundant, I suppose.<end>

segment.source: ::Salute and leave.::<end>
segment.target: ::Salute and leave.::<end>

segment.source: Thank you, sir. I'm glad the captain didn't forget about me. Now, there was something else I needed of you. <end>
segment.target: Thank you, sir. I'm glad the captain didn't forget about me. Now, there was something else I needed of you. <end>

segment.source: I'd love to chat, sir, but I have to leave. ::Salute and leave.::<end>
segment.target: I'd love to chat, sir, but I have to leave. ::Salute and leave.::<end>

segment.source: ::Remain silent and open the package.::<end>
segment.target: ::Remain silent and open the package.::<end>

segment.source: Heh, who are you? Actually, it doesn't matter anyway. ::He waves you away.::<end>
segment.target: Heh, who are you? Actually, it doesn't matter anyway. ::He waves you away.::<end>

segment.source: Corporal. I'm sure you'd be delighted to know that I've received new equipment you can spend your blues on.<end>
segment.target: Corporal. I'm sure you'd be delighted to know that I've received new equipment you can spend your blues on.<end>

segment.source: Show me what you got. ::Barter.::<end>
segment.target: Show me what you got. ::Barter.::<end>

segment.source: Later. I had some questions first.<end>
segment.target: Later. I had some questions first.<end>

segment.source: Oh?<end>
segment.target: Oh?<end>

segment.source:
::You approach the man you believe to be Staff Sergeant Fraser. You stand still and salute him, and he returns it. During this brief salute, the two of you get the chance to take look at it each other. The first thing you notice is his thin but impressively long nose sitting between his brown eyes. Beneath it, you see jagged lips slowly reshape themselves into a condescending smile, for he too must've noticed something on you that caused that smirk. Then, he opens his mouth to deliver a high-pitched, nasal voice that borders on being feminine, and thus the conversation begins.::
At ease, Corporal. I'm Staff Sergeant Eric Fraser. I am the quartermaster here at Fort Apogee, so if you need equipment or need to exchange currency, I am the one to come to. Now, Corporal... what'll it be?<end>
